policy: References informed taxonomy, adult scale, lateral proportions, fin placement, stripe boundaries, and visible material character only. No source pixels were sampled, traced, copied, hotlinked, or redistributed.

sources.title: Paracheirodon innesi species summary
sources.author: Rainer Froese and Daniel Pauly, editors
evidenceCues: Accepted scientific name is Paracheirodon innesi (Myers, 1936).
Maximum length is recorded as 2.5 cm standard length.
The species is a small freshwater pelagic tetra from blackwater and clearwater tributaries of the Solimoes River.

sources.title: Morphometrics of Paracheirodon innesi, image Painn_u7.jpg
sources.author: FishBase morphometrics contributors
evidenceCues: Measured reference specimen is 3.0 cm total length and 82.6 percent standard length.
Body depth is 26.0 percent of total length; head length is 18.5 percent; eye diameter is 45.9 percent of head length.
Predorsal, prepelvic, and preanal distances are 40.4, 38.7, and 50.9 percent of total length; fork length is 90.7 percent and caudal aspect ratio is 2.23588.

sources.title: Paracheirodon innesi, neon tetra, species profile
sources.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey Nonindigenous Aquatic Species Database
sources.author: U.S. Geological Survey
sources.license: U.S. federal government work; facts and citation only
evidenceCues: The profile reports an adult size of 4 cm.
Identification is tied to the Weitzman and Fink 1983 group revision and its distinguishing characters, key, and photographs.

sources.title: Visual pigment in fish iridocytes
sources.author: J. N. Lythgoe, Julia Shand, and R. G. Foster
sources.license: Copyright Springer Nature; no source imagery reused
evidenceCues: The bright lateral stripe includes the iris and is produced by iridophores between dermal collagen and muscle.
Regular guanine and cytoplasm layers change spacing in response to light, changing the reflected color.

sources.title: Paracheirodon innesi neon tetra.jpg
sources.author: SOK
sources.provenance: Author's own work, photographed 16 December 2019; original 4214 by 2194 file page.
evidenceCues: Slender compressed body, large seated eye, short snout, clear fins, small adipose fin, and symmetrical forked caudal.
Electric blue band begins at the eye and ends beneath the adipose region; the red band occupies only the posterior ventrolateral half.
Olive-translucent dorsum and silver belly separate the two saturated stripes.

sources.title: Paracheirodon innesi (aka).jpg
sources.author: Andre Karwath aka Aka
sources.provenance: Author's own macro photograph, 7 April 2007; original 2144 by 1116 file page.
evidenceCues: Full lateral silhouette corroborates body depth, fin origins, short peduncle, forked tail, and large eye.
The blue stripe arches gently high on the flank while the red stripe begins near midbody and reaches the caudal base.

sources.title: Neon tetra (Paracheirodon innesi) in an aquarium.webm
sources.author: The Nature Box
sources.view: multi-angle live aquarium motion, 1.5 to 2 cm juveniles
sources.provenance: Author's own work, recorded 15 January 2016; original 1920 by 1080, 2 minute 9 second file page.
evidenceCues: Live schooling motion is forward-led with small rapid tail beats and restrained body roll.
Multi-angle movement shows translucent fins and angle-dependent lateral-stripe brightness.
Juvenile size and non-orthographic motion prohibit direct adult proportion calibration.

viewCoverage.lateral: Strong: FishBase morphometrics and two exact licensed adult file pages constrain the side silhouette, fins, eye, and diagnostic stripe boundaries.
viewCoverage.motionAndMaterial: Moderate: an exact licensed aquarium video supports small-fish tail cadence, translucent fins, and angle-dependent iridescence qualitatively.
viewCoverage.topAndBodyWidth: Limited: lateral compression is visible in moving oblique views, but no calibrated orthographic top original was found.
viewCoverage.front: Limited: moving oblique frames provide qualitative corroboration only; no sharp orthographic frontal original was found.

referenceGradeRationale: Authoritative scale and detailed lateral morphometrics combine with multiple exact, licensed adult references and a licensed motion source. Top and front calibration remains intentionally uncertain because no verified orthographic sources were found.
